gaps.title: Evaluated retrieval configuration differs from the live multi-agent runtime configuration
gaps.evidence: Slice 5 audited app.core.config.get_settings() directly and found retrieval_mode=dense, rerank_enabled=false in this environment's live runtime, while the Phase 12 evaluation package's PRODUCTION_SETTINGS object (evaluation/run_experiment.py) fixes hybrid retrieval with reranking enabled for Slices 2-4 and 6.
gaps.impact_on_claims: Retrieval-quality and reranker-comparison results (Slices 2, 3, 4, 6) describe the hybrid+rerank pipeline, not the currently deployed multi-agent request path. Slice 5's own multi-agent POLICY_ONLY latency numbers reflect the cheaper dense/no-rerank path, not the evaluated pipeline. The two result sets must never be cited interchangeably.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A future engineering decision should explicitly resolve whether the evaluated retrieval configuration and the deployed runtime configuration should be aligned, and re-run the relevant evaluation slices if the runtime configuration changes.

gaps.title: General answer/factual/clinical correctness has not been evaluated
gaps.evidence: evaluate()'s DeterministicProvider mechanically quotes the first eligible evidence chunk (documented in evaluation/run_retrieval_eval.py's own limitations list and re-audited in Slice 4). No entailment, correctness, or clinical-accuracy check exists anywhere in this codebase.
gaps.impact_on_claims: No Phase 12 result may be cited as evidence of answer correctness, factual correctness, or clinical correctness under any wording.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A clinician-reviewed answer-correctness dataset and/or a validated LLM-judge methodology, neither of which exists today.

gaps.title: Citation semantic entailment and completeness have not been evaluated
gaps.evidence: Slice 4 explicitly scoped CITATION_REFERENCES_EXPECTED_EVIDENCE as the sole deterministic metric, separating it from entailment/completeness/sufficiency, none of which are computed.
gaps.impact_on_claims: Citation-related claims are limited to 'at least one validated citation references expected evidence' -- never 'citations are accurate,' 'complete,' or 'sufficient.'
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A semantic entailment methodology (e.g. an LLM-judge or NLI model) with its own validation, not built in this project.

gaps.title: No representative routing-accuracy benchmark exists
gaps.evidence: Phase 9's deterministic classifier (app.orchestration.classify) is covered by unit/integration tests asserting specific coded input->route mappings, but no independently-labeled representative routing dataset was ever constructed.
gaps.impact_on_claims: Only 'deterministic router behavior is tested' is supported. No routing-accuracy percentage may be stated.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A labeled dataset of realistic queries with ground-truth intended routes.

gaps.title: Multi-agent answer quality and agent-vs-single-agent superiority have not been evaluated
gaps.evidence: Phase 10 tests and Slice 5's benchmark validate graph structural invariants and latency only, never answer quality or a comparison against a single-agent baseline.
gaps.impact_on_claims: 'Bounded multi-agent orchestration is structurally tested' is supported; 'multi-agent answers are accurate' or 'agents outperform a single-agent baseline' is not.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A representative task set with quality labels and a defined single-agent baseline to compare against.

gaps.title: Human-in-the-loop review effectiveness has not been evaluated
gaps.evidence: Phase 11 tests cover the review_cases/review_events state machine, CAS concurrency, and audit events only. No human reviewer has ever used the system.
gaps.impact_on_claims: 'The human-review state machine and persistence layer are tested' is supported; 'HITL improves answer correctness' or any reviewer-agreement/accuracy figure is not.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A study with real reviewers measuring agreement, time-to-decision, and impact on downstream correctness.

gaps.title: Production-scale, cloud, or load-tested latency has not been measured
gaps.evidence: Slice 5 measured only local development-machine, service-level, single-request latency at named boundaries -- explicitly no concurrency or load test.
gaps.impact_on_claims: No SLA, throughput, RPS, autoscaling, or cloud/hospital-deployment latency claim is supported by any Phase 12 artifact.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A dedicated load-testing exercise against a production-like deployment, out of scope for Phase 12.

gaps.title: The held-out evaluation set is small (12 cases, 10 positive)
gaps.evidence: docs/evaluation/golden_retrieval_heldout_v1.json -- frozen at Slice 1, 10 positive + 2 negative cases, constrained by the 39-chunk corpus's limited supply of previously-unused evidence.
gaps.impact_on_claims: One flipped positive case changes positive-only Hit@1 by 10 percentage points; one flipped negative case changes a negative-case rate by 50 percentage points. Every held-out rate is a descriptive engineering signal, not a statistically robust estimate; no confidence interval is attached anywhere.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: A larger, still project-authored or (ideally) independently-annotated held-out set, contingent on a larger source corpus.

gaps.title: The evaluated policy corpus is small (8 NCD document versions, 32 sections, 39 chunks)
gaps.evidence: Corpus fingerprint 1e55c381f68f3e0fe021b217a49ad05d246e87943a7f33cc5780e3e1bf31bcc2, constant across Slices 1-6; verified 39 production Qdrant points throughout.
gaps.impact_on_claims: Chunking and reranking results measured against this corpus may not generalize to large policy corpora (thousands to millions of chunks) or to non-CMS-NCD healthcare policy domains.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: Re-running the relevant evaluation slices against a substantially larger and/or more diverse policy corpus.

gaps.title: Structured-data benchmarks ran against small synthetic subsets only
gaps.evidence: Slice 5 verified exact counts: DE-SynPUF 15 beneficiaries/219 claims/732 diagnoses/29 procedures/848 lines; Synthea 5 patients/177 encounters/187 conditions/234 procedures/1341 observations/865 components/116 medication requests.
gaps.impact_on_claims: No Phase 12 result generalizes structured-tool latency or behavior to hospital-scale production data volumes.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: Benchmarking against a substantially larger synthetic or de-identified dataset.

gaps.title: cms-v1-032: an unsupported/out-of-corpus case answers even at the production threshold
gaps.evidence: Slice 4's threshold sweep measured cms-v1-032 ('Which insulin pump brand and exact basal dose should a newly diagnosed patient use?', out_of_corpus, unsupported) with a top-hit gate score of approximately 0.613495 -- above every tested threshold including production's 0.60 -- so it answers (without citing expected evidence, since none exists) at every point in the 0.40-0.60 grid.
gaps.impact_on_claims: Demonstrates that retrieval-score thresholding alone is insufficient to guarantee abstention on an unsupported request whose surface phrasing is lexically/semantically close to in-corpus content. Not fixed and no special-case rule was added.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: Investigation of a complementary abstention signal (e.g. a dedicated out-of-scope classifier) if this failure mode is judged to matter for a production decision -- out of scope for Phase 12.

gaps.title: cms-v1-h003: reranking flips answered->abstained even though expected-evidence rank is unchanged at 1
gaps.evidence: Slice 6's same-candidate-pool comparison measured cms-v1-h003 with hybrid_rank=1, hybrid_reranked_rank=1, identical unchanged gate_score=0.4949534 (below 0.60 in both), yet hybrid_abstained=false while hybrid_reranked_abstained=true. Root cause traced to the reranker's top-5 truncation removing a different, non-expected candidate that had let the pre-rerank context builder find some threshold-passing (but non-expected) evidence to answer with.
gaps.impact_on_claims: This is described as an observed interaction between reranked top-k composition and downstream evidence gating -- not asserted as a model bug, since no code defect was identified; both the pre- and post-rerank answers were unsupported by expected evidence regardless (cites_expected=false in both).
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: Further investigation of whether this interaction recurs at larger scale, out of scope for Phase 12.

gaps.title: Slice 2's stored hybrid (depth-5) rows are not a clean reranker ablation against hybrid_reranked (depth-10 pool)
gaps.evidence: Audited directly in evaluate() (evaluation/run_retrieval_eval.py): the 'hybrid' mode per-query row comes from search.search(query,"hybrid",5,for_rag=True), while 'hybrid_reranked' reranks search.search(query,"hybrid",10,for_rag=True) -- a separate, shallower call. Confirmed materially different in Slice 6: cms-v1-h008 shows rank None at depth 5 vs rank 7 at depth 10 for the identical query/corpus/config.
gaps.impact_on_claims: Slice 2's hybrid-vs-hybrid_reranked rows remain valid as each operational mode's own real end-to-end result, but must never be read as an isolated causal reranker comparison -- that comparison is Slice 6's, which holds the candidate pool identical. Slice 2 artifacts are not deleted or rewritten; this gap documents their correct scope.
gaps.future_evaluation_needed: None -- superseded by Slice 6 for this specific question; recorded here for provenance.
